 Southwest Florida is heading into a changing weather pattern this week. After another stretch of beautiful weather, increasing moisture and a strengthening northeast breeze will bring more clouds and a few opportunities for showers.
 High pressure will remain in control across the eastern United States, helping keep temperatures near seasonal averages. However, a developing disturbance moving across the Gulf and Florida will bring a gradual increase in rain chances, especially by the middle of the week.
 Monday: Sunshine, clouds and a few showers possible
 Monday will start on a pleasant note, with morning temperatures generally in the upper 50s and lower 60s across Southwest Florida.
 We'll see a mix of sunshine and clouds throughout the day, with afternoon highs climbing into the upper 70s and lower 80s.
 A stray shower cannot be ruled out, mainly across inland locations, but most communities should stay dry. Northeast winds will gradually increase, with sustained speeds between 5 and 15 mph.
 Tuesday: Increasing clouds and a few showers
 Our weather pattern begins to change Monday night into Tuesday as a disturbance moves eastward across the Gulf of America and Florida.
 This system will help bring additional moisture into the region, increasing cloud coverage and creating the potential for a few passing showers.
 Rain chances will increase to around 20% Tuesday. Most of the area will likely remain dry, but a few inland communities could see a passing shower.
 Temperatures will remain comfortable, with highs generally in the upper 70s.
 Wednesday and Thursday: Breezy with isolated showers
 The breezy pattern will stick around through much of the second half of the week.
 High pressure strengthening across the eastern United States will help tighten the pressure gradient across Florida, resulting in persistent northeast winds.
 Wind gusts could approach 25 to 30 mph Wednesday and Thursday, especially along the coast and over the local waters.
 With additional moisture filtering in from the Atlantic, a few showers will be possible each afternoon, mainly inland. Rain chances will reach around 30% Wednesday through Friday.
 These are not widespread rain chances, and many communities will likely remain dry.
 Looking ahead to the weekend
 Conditions should gradually become less breezy heading into the weekend.
 Rain chances will decrease to around 20% Saturday and Sunday, with a mix of sunshine and clouds expected.
 Temperatures will remain warm, with afternoon highs climbing into the lower 80s. Overnight lows will generally settle into the middle and upper 60s.
